The returns quality column gives the reason for every n/a and tags every approximation. Common tags:
- since_data_inception: the return runs from the entity's first snapshot, not from when the account opened.
- configured_inception: the window starts at an inception date set in the config.
- staggered_inception: the entity's parts began on different dates.
- accounts_grain_meaningless: this source's accounts are set to show values without returns (config returns_policy_overrides); read a coarser view.
- empty_bucket, carried_forward: no snapshot fell in the bucket; the value is carried from before it.
- boundary_same_snapshot: the bucket starts and ends on the same snapshot.
- stale_snapshot: the end value rests on a snapshot much older than the entity's usual gap; the feed may have stopped.
- dietz_degenerate: the bucket's approximation has no defined value.
- post_exit_residue: money left nearly all of the entity; twr leaves out the periods on what remained, while gain and mwr still count its income.
- nonpositive_base: a loan or a net-negative entity; a return means nothing.
- mwr_no_flows: no money moved in or out, so there is no money-weighted return; read twr.
- mwr_no_sign_change, mwr_nonunique, mwr_no_converge: the money-weighted return has no single answer.
- mwr_negative_net_capital: the money put in, net, is zero or less.
- unmatched_transfers=N: N transfers found no matching leg on another account.
- cross_source_netted=N: N transfer pairs the load stored netted out inside the entity, across sources or inside one source.
- nav_only, nav_only_capital_call_risk: a source that reports values only (private funds); the return is rough.
- pre_fx_history: part of the window lies before the exchange-rate history begins.
- flows_before_inception: money moved before the date the measurement starts; it counts in no window.
- after_tax: the return is net of the fees and taxes paid.
- benchmark_start_clipped, benchmark_end_clipped: the benchmark's months start later or end sooner than the window; compared_from and compared_to say which days the figures cover.
- benchmark_gap: a month of the span has no return for a fund of the mix, so the benchmark has none.
- benchmark_partial_period: the benchmark's months start or end inside the bucket.
- benchmark_no_overlap: the window and the benchmark's months share no day.
- shadow_nonpositive: the flows took out more than the same money in the benchmark held.
- no_engine_row: (view=stated) the engine has no monthly row for a month of the stated period; the account's own tags follow.
- debt_first_seen: (view=bridge) a debt appeared with no matching cash, so net_saved falls once by what was already owed.
- debt_ended: (view=bridge) a debt left the history while still owed, so debt_repaid rises with no payment.
- debt_unpriced: (view=bridge) a debt has no rate to the currency; its fall is left to gain.
- bridge_gap: (view=bridge) net worth less returns' value is not the mortgages and cards; gain holds the difference.
- tracking_netted: (view=bridge) net_flow and onboarded had opposite signs, so the smaller size reads as a move into or out of tracking, in neither column.
Other tags name their reason the same way.

On spending view=fees, quality says what a row misses, beside the return's tags:
- no_mean_value: the mean value is not above zero, so there is no fee rate.
- part_window_value: the entity held a value on only part of the window.
- no_return: returns has no row for the entity, as for a plumbing cash account.
- unpriced_fees=N: N fee lines have no rate to the currency.

The gains quality column names each way a figure can be incomplete:
- sells_without_documents=N: N sales have no tax document or statement lot, and the lot engine rebuilt none, so realized misses them.
- sells_rebuilt=N: N sales are realized as the lot engine rebuilt them from the trades; no document states them.
- lots_without_gain=N: N realized lots state no gain, and not both proceeds and a cost basis.
- undated_lots=N: N lots state only a tax year and count at its last day.
- unmatched_lots=N: N lots name an instrument the account never held in a snapshot.
- in_kind_moves=N: N securities moved in or out of the account without a sale; each brings or takes its whole unrealized gain.
- corporate_actions=N: N mergers, splits or spin-offs turned one holding into another without a realized lot.
- basis_changed=N: N holdings began or stopped carrying a cost basis inside the period; their change is left out.
- accounts_unobserved=N: N accounts are missing from one end of the period while their source has a snapshot there; the snapshot left them out, or they closed.
- paid_in_basis: a private holding's cost basis is the capital paid in; cash paid back is not realized gain.
- onboarded_in_window=<source>: the source's data begins inside the period, so its start value is zero.
- seed_lots=N: the lot engine opened N lots of unknown cost for holdings the trades do not explain.
- implied_disposals=N: N times a snapshot held less than the trades explain; the lots left with no proceeds.
- snapshot_blips=N: N times a snapshot was off for less than 45 days; the lots stand as the trades left them.
- spliced: a rebuilt cost basis holds a lot whose cost a statement stated later.
- pooled: a rebuilt cost basis is a portfolio's pool, shared among its wallets by quantity.
- dated_by_settlement: rebuilt sales are dated by settlement, so a term near one year can be off.
- wash_sales_not_applied=N: N rebuilt losses fall within 30 days of a purchase; no wash sale rule was applied.
- fee_unvalued=N: N fees in a third currency had no rate and are left out of the cost or proceeds.
- basis_assumed_zero=N: under missing_basis=zero, N positions and lots took 0 for a cost no one states.
- fx_missing=N: N figures had no exchange rate and are left out.

The exposure quality column names what a figure rests on, each tag with the share of the row it covers (proxy=12%):
- proxy: another fund's composition stands in.
- declared: a declaration states it.
- aged: the composition is older than 35 days.
- forward: the composition is dated after the day.
- partial: the weights leave more than 3% unexplained, a forward states no legs, or a fund lies deeper than three levels.
- unmapped: a provider's label has no place in the vocabulary.
- by_name: a receipt's or a report line's sector or country comes from a share matched by name among all shares.
- opaque: a private equity fund nothing looks through; it reads diversified.
- undeclared: a private holding has no declaration of its exposure.
- unmatched: a listed security or fund no source describes.
- no_composition: a fund no composition and no declaration describes on the day, in the funds view.
- unknown: in the credit view: debt no rating, rating fund or known label of its fund's page describes.

In view=situs, quality gives the share of the row each basis of the situs covers (isin=80%):
- declared: a declaration states it.
- underlying: a depositary receipt reads as the share it stands for.
- isin: the country of the holding's ISIN prefix.
- domicile: a fund's domicile (the US for one that files N-PORT) or a security's, where it has no ISIN of a country.
- custody: cash or metal sits in its custodian's country (exposure.custody).
- country: the one country a declaration states for a private holding.
- unknown: none of these: a coin, cash at a custodian with no country, or a holding to declare.

The yield quality column names what a figure rests on, each tag with the share of the row's gross value it covers (stated=61%); a bare tag covers the whole row:
- implied: the yield is computed from the price.
- stated: a source states the rate.
- indicated: a dividend is the last payment at its frequency, or the filings'.
- realized: the figure comes from the transactions, where nothing else is known.
- declared: a ledger record states it.
- aged: a fund's composition is older than exposure allows.
- stale_price: a fund's lines are priced on their filing's day, not the day.
- floating: a floating note, which implies no yield, or a fund whose income resets with the rates: its lines or its filing's float for half of it or more, or its name says it floats.
- default: a bond is graded in default, or a fund holds lines in default or arrears; they imply nothing.
- thin: the amount was under a tenth of its mean on more than half the year's days, so it has no realized yield.
- partial: a figure covers part of the year: a position's realized yield covers the days it was held, fewer than the year's; or a payer twice a year shows one half's dividend, as the other half's rate is lost.
- units: a dividend per share may be in the units of its day: no whole factor explains how they changed since, or no account held it through a span since.
- unknown: no source and no record gives a figure.
- mixed: a total across currencies.

On income's forward views, basis says what an expected amount rests on (on projection each basis's share, declared=76% stated=24%):
- declared: a rate a ledger record states, a coupon by contract, a bill's discount.
- indicated: the last payment at its frequency, or the filings' dividends.
- stated: a rate a source states, held.
- forward: a stated, declared or indicated floating rate, moved along its currency's forward curve.
- reinvested: what a principal earns after a maturity.
- realized: last year's payments, where nothing else is known.
- unknown: nothing; the amount is zero.

Their quality column gives the share of the reinvested income each way of reinvesting earns (roll=100% roll_cash=0%), then shift=±Nbp where a shift moves the income:
- cash: the cash rule: the rate of the account's cash.
- roll: the roll rule: the forward rate of the holding's term plus its own spread.
- roll_constant: a roll at the holding's own implied yield, held constant, where its currency has no curve.
- roll_own: a roll at its current yield, else its stated rate, held constant, where it implies none.
- roll_cash: a roll into cash, where the holding has no yield at all.

On cashflow's projection, quality lists what a row rests on:
- projected: investment_income, principal_returned and vehicles_income are the income projection's.
- trailing: the other parts are monthly averages of the look-back.
- terms: a mortgage's instalments end at its terms' maturity.
- thin: the look-back holds under 6 months.
